questions.question: Write pseudo-code to declare an array of 5 temperatures and output the third temperature.

points.text: temps ← [18.5, 20.3, 22.1, 19.8, 21.0] OUTPUT temps[2] // Outputs 22.1 (third element, index 2)

questions.question: Write pseudo-code that finds the sum of all elements in the array [10, 20, 30, 40, 50].

points.text: numbers ← [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] total ← 0 FOR i ← 0 TO 4 total ← total + numbers[i] NEXT i OUTPUT total // 150

questions.question: A 2D array represents a 3x3 tic-tac-toe board. How would you access the centre square?

points.text: The centre square is at row 1, column 1: board[1][1]

questions.question: Define a record called Car with fields for make (string), model (string), year (integer), and price (real).

points.text: TYPE Car make AS STRING model AS STRING year AS INTEGER price AS REAL ENDTYPE

questions.question: Write pseudo-code that iterates through an array of names and outputs only the names that start with "A".

points.text: names ← ["Alice", "Bob", "Amy", "Charlie", "Anna"] FOR i ← 0 TO 4 IF SUBSTRING(names[i], 0, 1) = "A" THEN OUTPUT names[i] ENDIF NEXT i

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A program needs to store the names and test scores of 5 students. Explain why a record is more suitable than two separate arrays, and write pseudo-code to declare and use this data structure. [5 marks] <div class="

points.text: Using two separate arrays (one for names, one for scores) keeps related data in separate structures, making it harder to keep data together when sorting or passing to subroutines. A record groups related fields of different types into one unit. TYPE Student name : STRING score : INTEGER ENDTYPE declare students : ARRAY[1:5] OF Student students[1].name ← 'Alice' students[1].score ← 87 students[2].name ← 'Bob' students[2].score ← 72 This keeps each student's name and score together as a single unit, making the data easier to manage, sort, and pass to subroutines.
